newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai coffee market stalled as sellers hold off.
newsitem.headline: Thai coffee market stalled as sellers hold off.

text.p: The Thai coffee market was at a standstill as sellers kept supplies off the market and pushed for higher prices, trade sources said on Wednesday.

Thai robusta faq (fair average quality), the only grade exported by Thailand, was indicated at $1,375-1,450 per tonne FOB Bangkok. But sellers said they could not profit at current price levels and offered $1,500 per tonne and up.

"There is almost no activity in the market now because the price ideas of sellers and buyers are so different," said a Bangkok-based trader. "But Thai sellers are in a position that they can wait because almost all the 1996/97 crop was sold or committed," he said.
There were only about 8,000-10,000 tonnes of coffee left unsold for the season, according to trade sources.
Another trader said the market expected world coffee prices to improve as winter approaches in Brazil. Moreover, supplies of coffee, especially Arabica, were getting tighter.
"We expect that tight arabica supplies will have a spillover effect on robusta in term of demand," he said.
